extracted.intended_audience: students, practitioners, and researchers in corporate communication / public relations
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the functions, responsibilities, and component disciplines of corporate communication, intended to guide how organizations manage internal and external messaging, branding, reputation, and stakeholder relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote corporate profile (corporate branding)
rubrics_metrics.description: to promote the profile of the 'company behind the brand' (corporate branding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate branding seeks to create favourable associations and positive reputation with internal and external stakeholders; its purpose is to generate a positive halo over products and businesses and impart more favourable impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize identity/brand discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: to minimize discrepancies between the company's desired identity and brand features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should align the company's expressed identity with the brand features experienced by stakeholders to preserve coherence, credibility and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegate communication tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: to delegate tasks in communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should allocate responsibility for different communication activities to appropriate specialists or teams (e.g., media relations, investor relations, employee communication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulate and execute communication decision procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: to formulate and execute effective procedures to make decisions on communication matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate communication requires clear processes/routines for deciding what, when, and how to communicate across audiences and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobilize internal and external support for objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: to mobilize internal and external support for corporate objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication should build buy-in among employees, partners, communities and other stakeholders to support strategic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate communication with international partners
rubrics_metrics.description: to coordinate with international business firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-border operations require alignment of messages, local adaptations, and coordination between corporate and local communication functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the three principal communication clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Three principal clusters of task-planning and communication: management communication, marketing communication, and organizational communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure communication planning around these clusters: management communication (between management and audiences), marketing communication (advertising, direct mail, personal selling, sponsorship), and organizational communication (PR, investor relations, employee communication, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing communication channels and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing communication consists of product advertising, direct mail, personal selling, and sponsorship activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing communication typically receives the bulk of budgets and is focused on promoting products/services through paid and promotional channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational communication functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational communication consists of specialists in public relations, public affairs, investor relations, environmental communications, corporate advertising, and employee communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specialist functions translate corporate strategy into coherent messages for different stakeholder groups and help support management communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: When corporate branding is appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Research suggests corporate branding is appropriate when there is significant information asymmetry, customers are less informed, customers perceive high purchase risk, or company features are relevant to the purchase decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use corporate branding to provide reassurance and create favourable associations when product-level information is limited or risk is high; the corporate brand should add relevant credibility to product/service choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate identity (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate identity is the reality and uniqueness of an organization, integrally related to its external and internal image and reputation through corporate communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity work should reflect the actual distinctive attributes of the organization and be communicated consistently to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational identity (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational identity comprises characteristics that members believe are central, distinctive and enduring—attributes felt to be fundamental, uniquely descriptive, and persistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal communications and culture-building should reinforce these core attributes to maintain consistency between members' beliefs and external messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection of attributes that are seen as typical for continuity, centrality and uniqueness of the organization in the eyes of its members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and manage how members perceive the organization's central and unique attributes to ensure internal alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projected identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The self-presentations of the organization's attributes manifested in implicit and explicit signals broadcast to internal and external audiences through communication and symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signals (visual identity, messaging, behavior) consistently project the intended attributes to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired (ideal) identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The idealized picture that top managers hold of what the organization could evolve into under their leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership should communicate aspiration clearly but manage gaps between desired identity and current reality to avoid credibility problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applied identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The signals that an organization broadcasts both consciously and unconsciously through behaviors and initiatives at all levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational behaviors and initiatives must be aligned with communicated identity to avoid mixed messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate responsibility (CR) / CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate responsibility constitutes an organization's respect for society's interests, demonstrated by taking ownership of effects its activities have on key constituencies including customers, employees, shareholders, communities, and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CR communications should show how the company looks beyond the bottom line and addresses the social implications of its business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate reputation (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputations are aggregate perceptions by stakeholders of an organization's ability to fulfill their expectations (buyers, employees, investors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputation management aims to maintain or improve stakeholders' assessments by meeting expectations consistently across domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication (purpose and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis communication is designed to protect and defend an individual, company, or organization facing a public challenge to its reputation (e.g., investigations, allegations, media inquiries, lawsuits, regulatory violations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat crises as major events (natural or human-caused) that can have tangible or intangible devastation, significant financial impact, and affect multiple constituencies; rapid, coordinated response is required to protect reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal communication roles — Efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency: Internal communication is used primarily to disseminate information about corporate activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use channels and formats that reliably and quickly share necessary information to the right employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal communication roles — Shared meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Shared meaning: Internal communication is used to build a shared understanding among employees about corporate goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design messages and forums that foster common interpretations of strategy and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal communication roles — Connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Connectivity: Internal communication is used mainly to clarify the connectivity of the company's people and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight how roles, teams and processes interlink to improve coordination and sense of belonging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal communication roles — Satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfaction: Internal communication is used to improve job satisfaction throughout the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use communication to recognize contributions, explain decisions, and support employee morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor relations core functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of investor relations is to (1) comply with regulations, (2) create a favorable relationship with key financial audiences, and (3) contribute to building and maintaining the company's image and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IR communications must meet disclosure/regulatory requirements while shaping credible narratives for investors and analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations: integrate corporate messages
rubrics_metrics.description: PR specialists must incorporate broader corporate messages to convey the company's strategic positioning and ensure PR activities ultimately convey messages that distinguish the company vis-à-vis competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR planning should align tactical activities (sponsorships, events, media relations) with corporate strategic messages to communicate value to target audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues management
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues management is the set of organizational procedures, routines, personnel, and issues used to manage public concerns about company activities, often magnified by interest groups and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify strategic issues that compel company response—conflicts between identifiable groups over procedural or substantive distribution of positions or resources—and put routines in place to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations (cultivate relationships)
rubrics_metrics.description: To build better relationships with the media, organizations must cultivate positive relations with influential members of the media; this may be handled internally or by an external PR firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively engage, provide timely and accurate information, and maintain credibility with journalists and outlets to improve coverage quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company / spokesperson profiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Company/spokesperson profiling: select and prepare public faces considered authorities in their sector to ensure the organization is in the limelight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use credible spokespeople to represent the company; train them to deliver coherent corporate messages and handle media interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage external touchpoints and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing content of corporate websites and/or other external touch points; managing corporate publications for the external world and managing print media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all external channels (websites, publications, print) consistently reflect corporate messaging, branding and factual accuracy.
